doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Scottish youth bands and the Ellington high school competition
summary: He runs a growing youth band seminar in Scotland and takes part in Lincoln Center's high school Ellington competition.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I was just going to ask if you ever have occasion to get back to Scotland.

Yeah. I was there a year ago, a year past February. I have a high school band there. We started off doing a seminar in the summertime. We started off with like 15 kids. And now there’s 75 kids and there’s three different bands. There’s a band from like 8 years old to 11, and there’s another band from 11 to 14, and another band from 14 to 16 or 17. So now it’s grown and in fact, we’re trying to arrange for them to come to Lincoln Center. Because at Lincoln Center we have a high school competition — an Ellington competition. It started off with seven states. In fact it started off with just the three states around New York: New York, New Jersey and Connecticut. Then it grew to seven states. Now it’s the whole eastern part of the United States, all the way to the Mississippi. So now there’s 38 bands going to be at Lincoln Center next May. I’ll go out and do some clinics with that, and a couple of years ago I did some of the judging, last year I was a mentor which means you go up and play with the school bands and you sort of prime them for the competition. So it’s very interesting to do things like that. So I keep busy all the time.
